学.meaning: A <part>child</part> sits under a <part>blanket</part> with a torch, long past bedtime. A <part>sparkle</part> of ideas pops up over the blanket every time she turns a page. She isn't playing in there: she's trying to <kanji>study</kanji>.
学.on: A <sound>gag</sound>gle of geese honks outside the window, but she keeps on reading.
学.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>! <sound>Na</sound>an, please!' she calls from under the blanket, still reading about <sound>bu</sound>lldozers.

工.meaning: Two flat planks joined by one stout post: a workbench seen from the side. Saws, glue and wood shavings everywhere. Whatever you build on it, a birdhouse or a boat, you make it by hand, and that's <kanji>craft</kanji>.
工.on: On the workbench you carve an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne out of wood, sprinkles and all.

左.meaning: A <part>slash</part> crosses a <part>one</part>-plank arm reaching out over a <part>workbench</part>. A carpenter swings his hammer from that side only, and everyone else stands on the other side to be safe. He works with his <kanji>left</kanji> hand.
左.on: At lunch the carpenter eats one <sound>sar</sound>dine, holding it in his left hand.
左.kun: At the beach he hangs his shoe by the <sound>hee</sound>l, feeds a <sound>du</sound>ck and swims out to the <sound>ree</sound>f, always on the left.

穴.meaning: A <part>roof</part> covers a dark doorway whose sides spread like an <part>eight</part>. It's not a house, though. Something lives down there, and only its glowing eyes peek out. It's a burrow, a deep <kanji>hole</kanji>.
穴.on: You squirt <sound>ketch</sound>up into the hole to lure it out.
穴.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' A paw shoots up and drags a whole <sound>na</sound>an down the hole.

空.meaning: A <part>workbench</part> sits right under a <part>hole</part> in the roof. Every night the tools vanish up through it, one by one. By morning there's nothing left but sky showing through. The bench is <kanji>empty</kanji>.
空.on: A pigeon flies down through the hole, finds nothing on the bench and lets out a long, sad '<sound>coo</sound>'.
空.kun: Through the hole you see the sky: a <sound>so</sound>fa floats past, and a cheerleader on it yells '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

目.meaning: A tall box with two bars across the inside. Tip your head to the side and it's an almond shape with lids top and bottom and a pupil in the middle. It blinks. It's watching you steal a cookie. It's an <kanji>eye</kanji>.
目.on: You tiptoe away, one foot in a soft <sound>moc</sound>casin, but the eye follows you.
目.kun: The eye rolls at your cookie stealing and sighs, '<sound>Meh</sound>.'

貝.meaning: A big <part>eye</part> peeks out between the two halves of a shell that sits on <part>eight</part>-shaped little feet. It shuffles across the sand, snaps shut when you come near and opens again when you leave. It's a <kanji>shellfish</kanji>.
貝.on: A kid on a <sound>bi</sound>ke rides along the beach, and the shellfish snaps shut.
貝.kun: The shellfish ties a string to its shell and flies it like a <sound>ki</sound>te over the beach.

側.meaning: A <part>shellfish</part> is squeezed between a <part>coat hook</part> on its left and a <part>dagger</part> on its right. Whichever way it shuffles, something pointy waits there. It picks the hook, the friendlier <kanji>side</kanji>.
側.on: Then someone hangs a smelly <sound>sock</sound> on the hook, and the shellfish switches sides.
側.kun: On the other side, a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic makes it cry '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

北.meaning: A <part>climbing pole</part> and a <part>spoon</part> stand back to back, both shivering. They kept walking up the map until the snow reached their knees and a polar bear started staring at the spoon. They've gone too far <kanji>north</kanji>.
北.on: To warm up, they share a <sound>ho</sound>tdog with a frozen <sound>cu</sound>ckoo.
北.kun: The spoon digs up a frozen <sound>key</sound> sticking out of a <sound>tu</sound>b of snow.

西.meaning: A flat bar on top, then a box with two legs dangling inside, like a traveller hanging in a doorway. Every evening he watches the sun sink, then walks after it, always toward the <kanji>west</kanji>.
西.on: He carries his gold in a little steel <sound>sa</sound>fe strapped to his back.
西.kun: At sunset he kneels, one k<sound>nee</sound> in the dust and a <sound>shee</sound>p beside him, to watch the sun go.

自.meaning: An <part>eye</part> with a little tuft of hair on top stares into a mirror for hours, combing the tuft. It takes a selfie, then another, then ten more. It only ever looks at one thing: <kanji>oneself</kanji>.
自.on: It even paints its own face on the side of its <sound>jee</sound>p.
自.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat carves its own face on a <sound>zu</sound>cchini, then on a <sound>ca</sound>rp, then cheers for itself: '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

見.meaning: A huge <part>eye</part> walks around town on two skinny <part>legs</part>. It doesn't talk or eat. It just stops and stares at everything: shop windows, clouds, your lunch. All it wants to do is <kanji>see</kanji>.
見.on: It walks up to the <sound>ken</sound>nel and stares at the puppies for an hour.
見.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> stare right back at it.

南.meaning: A <part>ten</part> signpost points the way above a big <part>frame</part> of a beach hut. Inside, a goat with <part>horns</part> hangs wet swimsuits on a <part>drying rack</part>. It's hot, the sea is warm and everything dries in a minute: you've come far <kanji>south</kanji>.
南.on: The goat bakes a puffy <sound>naan</sound> on a hot stone in the sun.
南.kun: On the hot sand, a <sound>mee</sound>rkat hands a <sound>na</sound>an to another <sound>mee</sound>rkat.

斗.meaning: Two dots beside a cross with a long handle: a ladle for scooping water. Look up on a clear night and seven stars make the same shape, a giant ladle hanging in the sky. It's the <kanji>Big Dipper</kanji>.
斗.on: A <sound>to</sound>tem pole points up at the stars, its top carved like a ladle.

料.meaning: A canteen cook weighs one <part>ladle</part> of <part>rice</part> onto a tray, and the tray stays locked until a coin clinks into its slot. No coin, no lunch: every ladle has its <kanji>fee</kanji>.
料.on: At the <sound>ryo</sound>kan, the rice at dinner costs extra: one coin per ladle.

有.meaning: A <part>slash</part> and a <part>one</part>-plank arm make a hand that reaches up and grabs the <part>moon</part> right out of the sky. 'Mine now,' says the hand, tucking it under its arm. There's only one moon, and he gets to <kanji>possess</kanji> it.
有.on: A <sound>u</sound>nicorn gallops up and asks to borrow the moon for one night.
有.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' he says. 'Look, <sound>Roo</sound>, I have the moon!' and shows it to his kangaroo.

祖.meaning: A <part>lamppost</part> glows beside a stone: an <part>eye</part> carved on a <part>one</part>-plank base. Every evening the family lights the lamp, and the stone eye seems to watch over them the way great-great-grandma did. It's a stone for an <kanji>ancestor</kanji>.
祖.on: Great-great-grandma's old <sound>so</sound>fa still stands by the stone, and nobody else sits in it.

斤.meaning: Two slanted strokes at the top, a flat bar, and a long handle down to the ground. A woodcutter lifts it, swings it, and thunk: the log splits in two. It's a heavy <kanji>axe</kanji>.
斤.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher lands on the axe handle and watches the log split.

戸.meaning: A <part>one</part>-plank lintel sits on top of a <part>flag</part>-shaped frame that swings on its hinge. It's one panel, not two like a gate. Knock on it, push it, slam it: it's a <kanji>door</kanji>.
戸.on: A sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala hangs off the door handle and swings back and forth with it.
戸.kun: A <sound>to</sound>tem pole is far too tall to fit through the door, so it waits outside.

所.meaning: A <part>door</part> with an <part>axe</part> leaning beside it. Nobody knocks here: they chop. Hang the axe on the wall, light the fire, and this little cabin becomes your favourite <kanji>place</kanji>.
所.on: Behind the door is a tiny <sound>sho</sound>p that sells only firewood.
所.kun: A <sound>to</sound>tem pole, a <sound>ko</sound>ala and a <sound>ro</sound>dent live in the cabin too, each in its own spot.

近.meaning: An <part>axe</part> slides down a <part>ramp</part>, closer and closer to your toes. You step back. It slides again. Run! It's getting much too <kanji>near</kanji>.
近.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher swoops down the ramp right behind it, just as close.
近.kun: A <sound>chee</sound>tah sneaks right up next to you, close enough to grab your <sound>ca</sound>r keys.

止.meaning: A post with a short arm on its right and a long flat base along the ground: a white line painted across the road, with a sign beside it. Cars roll up, see the line and brake hard. This is where you <kanji>stop</kanji>.
止.on: A knight holds up his <sound>shi</sound>eld at the line, and every car stops for him.
止.kun: A <sound>to</sound>tem pole falls across the road, a kid yells '<sound>Ma</sound>!', and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> stops dead.

足.meaning: A round <part>mouth</part> of a kneecap sits on top, and under it a <part>stop</part> line where the foot plants flat on the ground. Kneecap, shin, foot: march, kick, hop. It's a <kanji>leg</kanji>.
足.on: Pull a smelly <sound>sock</sound> over the foot, and the whole leg is ready to go.
足.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' A <sound>shee</sound>p has stepped right on your foot.

元.meaning: <part>two</part> short lines on top and a pair of <part>legs</part> underneath: a baby standing up for the very first time, arms out. Wobble, wobble, one step. Every long walk starts right here, at the <kanji>beginning</kanji>.
元.on: 'Get up and go, <sound>Gen</sound>!' the family cheers, as baby Gen takes that first step.
元.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>le digs all the way back to where it started, under the <sound>to</sound>tem pole.

社.meaning: A <part>lamppost</part> lights up a mound of <part>soil</part> where workers dig the base of a new office tower. Hard hats, coffee, a big sign with a logo: they all work for the same <kanji>company</kanji>.
社.on: At lunch the whole office plays with a <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock in the car park.
社.kun: '<sound>Yah</sound>!' A <sound>shee</sound>p and a <sound>ro</sound>dent bow to a tiny wooden house under the lamppost: a shrine.

員.meaning: A <part>mouth</part> sits on top of a <part>shellfish</part> behind the fish counter, shouting 'Next!' all day. It doesn't own the shop. It wears a name badge and gets paid every Friday. It's an <kanji>employee</kanji>.
員.on: It writes down every order in blue <sound>in</sound>k on the back of its shell.

閉.meaning: Inside the <part>gate</part>, a <part>one</part>-plank bar is jammed across with a <part>crowbar</part>, and a <part>slash</part> of rope is tied round it. Push all you like, those doors won't budge. The gate is <kanji>closed</kanji>.
閉.on: A big pile of <sound>hay</sound> is stacked against the gate too, just to be sure.
閉.kun: A <sound>to</sound>tem pole, a <sound>jee</sound>p and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> wait outside the shut gate.

払.meaning: An <part>anchor</part>-shaped hand reaches out, an <part>elbow</part> crooked beside it, and slides a coin across the counter. The shopkeeper bites it to check it's real. Coin out, goods in: that's how you <kanji>pay</kanji>.
払.on: You pay for a <sound>fu</sound>ton, and the dust inside it makes you sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
払.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the shopkeeper as your coin lands, and a cheerleader shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>-rah!'

午.meaning: A <part>drying rack</part> stands in the yard with a <part>slash</part> of a stick leaning on top. The sun is right overhead, so the rack has almost no shadow and the sheets dry fast. It's twelve o'clock: <kanji>noon</kanji>.
午.on: At noon you jump in the pool wearing your <sound>go</sound>ggles.
午.kun: A horse trots up to the drying rack, munches the sheets and sighs: '<sound>Uma</sound>mi!'

後.meaning: A <part>chairlift</part> on the left. On the right, a <part>twist</part> of rope ties a <part>folding chair</part> to the last seat, so it bumps along at the very end. Everyone else gets to the top first. That chair is always <kanji>behind</kanji>.
後.on: Its rider wears <sound>go</sound>ggles against the snow kicked up by everyone ahead.
後.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' the rider yells, stuck behind a <sound>to</sound>tem pole on the seat in front.
